crm_notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for EditShift's IDE copilot product. Primary goal: predictable low-latency completions during peak developer hours (internal dev teams + early customers). Wants model pinning per-channel and burst policies for synchronized morning/afternoon peaks.

Background: EditShift builds an embeddable copilot SDK used by engineering teams at mid-size SaaS customers. Currently on multi-tenant hosted LLMs but seeing cost/latency variability during synchronized office hours (9-11am and 3-5pm PST). Looking for Dedicated to guarantee throughput and simpler SLAs for customers.

Technical requirements / constraints:
- Target first-token latency: <= 120ms median for single-token streaming in IDE (goal <100ms).
- Sustained p95 latency for completions: <= 250ms across 512 token windows.
- Peak concurrency: ~350 active developer sessions; burst headroom to 800 for product launches and internal all-hands testing.
- Throughput target: 1.2k tokens/sec sustained across pool during peaks; autoscale/burst to 3k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Model needs: multi-model routing (gpt-like open models + quantized variants), ability to pin model version per-customer/org, quick rollback capability.
- Feature needs: streaming token-by-token low-latency, session KV cache support, and token-level cost breakdowns for internal billing.
- Security: SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS integration for key control, audit logs and 90-day request retention, EU data residency for some enterprise customers.

Recent activity (timeline):
- 2025-01-10: Intro call (AE Casey, CTO Aaron Lee). Covered product fit and high-level load profile. Aaron: "can't tolerate spikes that break the dev experience."
- 2025-01-22: Technical deep-dive with SE Maya. Discussed KV cache, batching, and streaming latency tradeoffs. Maya demoed runtime options. (ff_1a2b3c link).
- 2025-01-28: Security questionnaire sent; EditShift provided SOC2 report and preliminary KMS details. Drive: editshift-security-answers.pdf.
- 2025-02-03: Internal capacity planning workshop with Redwood solutions team; sketched POC topology: 2-node dedicated pool + burst autoscale to 5 nodes.
- 2025-02-10: Pricing deck shared (drive link). Finance asked for ARR band and commit terms.
- 2025-02-13: Follow-up meeting to align POC metrics; agreed on success criteria and measurement plan.

POC scope / success criteria:
- 2-week POC on Redwood Dedicated in us-west with VPC peering and SSO integration.
- Simulate 50 concurrent devs (baseline) and a staged ramp to 350, validate median p50/p95 latencies, KV cache hit rates, and per-token cost metrics.
- Validate model pinning and rollback flow for one enterprise customer profile.
- Confirm burst policy behavior during 15-minute surge tests (target: auto-burst to handle 2.5x baseline without >2x p95 degradation).

Quotes / caller notes:
- Aaron Lee (CTO): "Even a few seconds of lag in the IDE kills adoption. We need predictable latency more than lowest cost."
- Eng lead Priya: "Token cost transparency is critical — we bill customers per-synced-minute and need per-route breakdowns."

Open questions / blockers:
- KMS integration: customer legal wants explicit confirmation on key custody model and HSM support.
- EU residency: need a clear plan for routing EU-stored customer data to eu-west dedicated pools.
- Pricing: looking for 12-month commit pricing with burst credits; finance needs a worked example for 300-seat org.

Next steps (short):
- Casey to send formal POC SOW and provisioning checklist by 2025-02-17.
- SE Maya to prepare a simulated load script and sample dashboards for POC metrics.
- Security: schedule KMS/architecture call with security engineering (target week of 2025-02-20).

Notes tone: shorthand, action-oriented. Key contacts: Aaron Lee (CTO), Priya Narang (Eng Lead), Casey Nguyen (AE), Maya Thompson (SE).
